title: fix(mcp)!: the stdio data bridge refuses a disabled package's data to every caller, system included
body:
repo:objectstack#3 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibyUSf2nKJWW6qBemSU

<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6JaoPh7eWmxwT5Pz7xHsDL4CM8)_

Fixes #36689

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no skill under `skills/**` says the stdio bridge serves a disabled package's data, to a system context or on any host; `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` row 15 now says the bypass covers API exposure only

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：通过本地 MCP 通道连上来的 AI 客户端，即使用的是系统身份、或宿主没有协议服务，也再也读写不到已停用软件包里的数据；停用前后的其它行为不变。
- 为什么做：属于「停用包之后处处都看不到它」专题，按你在卡上的裁决（和其它数据入口一致），把本地通道这扇门也关上。
- 出错会怎样：最坏是本地通道对某个本应可用的对象误报「软件包已停用」，重新启用该包即可恢复；改动可直接撤回。
- 要你做什么：无。

## What changes

Ruling: 7212906605 (letter A, 「是，和 callData 一致」).

`enforceApiExposure` (`packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts`) now asks the disabled-package question **first, of every caller**, before its system-context bypass:

- The question is the engine registry's `isObjectPackageDisabled`, read through `registryObjectPackageDisabled` (`@objectstack/core`), the predicate `callData` asks since the #35526 ruling. A new `StdioObjectReads.isObjectPackageDisabled` member carries it, built by `engineObjectPackageDisabled(engine)`, which reads the registry at each use. The refusal is the data plane's own `objectPackageDisabledError` (`404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`, the object named). No second copy of either.
- It covers the addressed object on every verb, and every nested-relation condition's target at every hop (the walk already calls `enforceApiExposure` per hop). A hop refusal carries the condition's position as `param` (`where.c_ref.b2_ref`), as `callData`'s does.
- Because the question is asked of the registry, not of the protocol's by-name read, a host with no `protocol` service refuses too.
- The `objectstack://` record resource gate in `plugin.ts` gets the same predicate.
- **[R1, M1]** `query_records` `expand`: `stdioExpandMap` asks the same registry question of each expansion target and withholds a disabled package's target (the row is served, the related record is not), on every host and for every caller. That is how the protocol arm of `callData` treats it (`servesExpansionTarget`). `callData`'s no-protocol fallback refuses `expand` with 501 instead; this door keeps its existing withhold posture, which its docblock already stated.
- **[R1, S1]** The relation walk reads the filtered object's field map from the engine registry first (`engineObjectDefinition(engine)`, `registry.getObject`), as `callData`'s walk reads it (`resolveWriteResponseSchema`), and falls back to the protocol read / metadata copy as before. So a condition the engine lowers is found even where neither the protocol nor the metadata copy holds the definition.
- A system context still skips the **exposure** question (`apiEnabled` / `apiMethods`), unchanged.

`content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` row 15 now says the bridge's bypass covers API exposure only, never the disabled-package refusal. The census register is unchanged (`enforceApiExposure` still holds one `isSystem` read). Patch changeset on `@objectstack/mcp`, with both declaration lines and an ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker.

## Tests

New `stdio-data-bridge.disabled-package-every-caller.test.ts`, on a **real** `ObjectQL` over in-memory SQLite, with the package disabled and re-enabled on the real registry: {host with a protocol service, host with none} × {system context, member} × {each of the six verbs on the addressed object, a one-hop and a two-hop relation condition with the stored value and another value}, plus a re-enable control per host (the row comes back; the two-hop condition counts 1 for the stored value and 0 for another) and the record-resource gate for a system context. **[R1]** Added: `expand` into the disabled object on both hosts × both callers, each with a re-enable control that shows the expansion served; and the one-hop / two-hop condition with **no** protocol definition and **no** metadata copy on both hosts × both callers, plus a re-enable control on each host that counts 1 / 0. 52 cases.

The three pins the review named, as it said:

| Pin | Disposition |
|:--|:--|
| `merged-object-reads.test.ts` "the record resource's gate refuses it too, and the system caller is still let through" | **Flipped on purpose**: the system caller is now refused, with a re-enable control that lets it through again |
| `exposure.test.ts` "bypasses for a system context, as callData does" | Unchanged and green: the package question reads the registry, never `metadataService.getObject`, so no metadata read lands before the dispatch |
| `relation-condition-target-exposure.test.ts` "CONTROL a system context is not asked the exposure question at any hop" | Unchanged and green |

<details><summary>Before / after, on the new file (base 7ad103a6 source restored over the committed tests)</summary>

Before the fix: **29 failed / 9 passed (38)**. After: **38 / 38**.

Measured on base, per cell:

- **System context, either host**: every verb on the addressed object was served (query, get, update, remove, aggregate; an `update` really wrote: the row read back `renamed`), and both relation hops were served. On the protocol host, `create` came back refused on base; read as the post-write strip's by-name read throwing after the insert, not measured further.
- **Member, host with no protocol service**: every verb and both hops were served. This is the reachable half.
- **Member, host with a protocol service**: already refused on base (the protocol's by-name read); the hop refusals lacked `param` only.
- The re-enable controls' two-hop count (1 / 0) passed on base as well, as a control should.

**[R1]** The delta against the first head (`7c110d9f`'s `stdio-data-bridge.ts` restored over the R1 tests): **10 failed / 42 passed (52)**, exactly the new cells: `expand` on the no-protocol host for both callers (the related record, `secret_note` included, was served), and all eight no-copy hop cells on both hosts (the condition was lowered, never asked). At `a8b989b7`: **52 / 52**.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- N1 of the contract record (`list_objects` / `describe_object` on a no-protocol host list a disabled package's objects: schema, not data) is left out of this PR and filed as #37904.
- The system-principal half has no live producer today: the stdio transport's principal comes from an API key and is never a system context. It is hardening. The no-protocol-host half is reachable.
- In the harness, the protocol's metadata store is not wired, so its by-name read answers `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` for an enabled object and the bridge falls back to the metadata copy, as on an outage. Disabled, it still throws `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` first. The registry question fires before either.

## Verification

Read first, by risk:

1. `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts`, the head of `enforceApiExposure`: the new refusal sits above `if (context?.isSystem) return;`.
2. `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts`, `stdioExpandMap` (the new withhold) and `enforceRelationTargetExposure` (the engine field map first).
3. `packages/mcp/src/plugin.ts`, `gateReads` for the record resource.

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/mcp exec vitest run src/stdio-data-bridge.disabled-package-every-caller.test.ts` shows 52 passed; restore `stdio-data-bridge.ts` and `plugin.ts` from `origin/main` and the same command fails (the R1 cells and the original 29).
